A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CogCoM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title, formatting, and appendix numbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original CogCoM benchmark evaluations, CoM-test learning curves, inference-time measurements, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds a training-data ablation, inference-turn measurements, and analysis of successful and unsuccessful reasoning paths.

M1.justification: The six manipulations, annotation-and-DFS pipeline, memory-based CogVLM architecture, and training objectives are retained. The four-turn training limit is newly disclosed; backtracking and reinforcement learning are future-work suggestions, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Section 5.4 adds MathVista to quantitative evaluation alongside TextVQA and MM-Vet. MathVista was already an annotation source in v2, so this extends evaluation coverage within an existing mathematical-reasoning domain. Earlier benchmarks and data sources remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Monkey and LLaVA-1.5 to the VQA comparison, and Table 3 adds Monkey to MM-Vet. LLaVA-1.5 already appeared in v2 Table 3; its participation in Table 1 is new. Grounding comparators are unchanged.

E3.justification: The new ablation removes 70K CoM examples while reportedly holding other settings fixed. Section 3.2 also changes the manual-annotation count from 6K to 7K, although the abstract still says 6K. This establishes a reported count revision, not that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct test of CoM training data's contribution through a controlled removal ablation on three benchmarks. Appendix D additionally examines multi-image inference turns, path quality, and successful versus unsuccessful generation across image classes. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence beyond v2's learning curves, timing analysis, and examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The new turn averages and class-frequency plot are descriptive results, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing CogCoM benchmark scores remain unchanged. Table 3 revises LLaVA-1.5's MM-Vet/POPE scores from 36.3/84.5 to 39.4/85.0. New Table 4 reports without/with-CoM scores of 64.5/71.1 on TextVQA, 45.9/46.1 on MM-Vet, and 34.8/35.7 on MathVista. Additional baseline entries and Appendix D's turn statistics and class-dependent findings extend the results.

T1.justification: The formal CoM structure, attention equations, synthesis algorithm, and reasoning-score formulas are retained. Reordering the parameter glossary and adjusting index typography clarify presentation without changing the mathematical relations. No new assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central claims about interpretable manipulation-based reasoning and the 17B model's benchmark performance remain. The introduction removes the unconditional error-free data claim, and the introduction and conclusion increase the claimed mathematical annotation contribution from 6K to 7K, inconsistently with the retained abstract.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies positive-path correctness by acknowledging oversized grounding boxes, interprets poorer generation success for small or uncommon objects as tool limitations, and discusses backtracking's computational tradeoff and possible reinforcement learning from negative paths. Existing limitations concerning diversity, visual-tool errors, and image-reinput overhead remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future release promise with a stated repository location for code, model, and data. Appendix D.1 newly discloses a four-turn training cap to prevent out-of-memory errors and elaborates quality control. The existing hardware, optimizer, learning-rate, and training-budget table is unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning against close alternatives, including ViperGPT, DualFocus, VPD, VisProg, Ferret-v2, video reasoning, and the already cited V*. It explains shared ideas and differences in training, tool use, and image manipulation. The earlier broad survey moves to Section 6, with CleverFlamingo omitted.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, edits the abstract, introduction, terminology, and limitations, and moves general related work from Appendix A into the main text. Appendices are reorganized and acknowledgments added, while most existing technical exposition and its sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds ablation Table 4 and the class-frequency Figure 7, extends Tables 1 and 3 with baseline rows, and adopts ICLR formatting. Existing diagrams, learning curves, annotation illustrations, and qualitative examples are retained with resizing, reflow, or renumbering.

improvement.justification: Table 4 provides more direct evidence for the contribution of CoM training data, while Appendix D improves transparency about generation failures and practical inference behavior. Closer prior-work comparisons also clarify the contribution. These benefits outweigh the new 6K/7K annotation-count inconsistency, but the limited controls and absence of uncertainty for small reported differences keep the overall improvement modest.
